Apex gave a force majeure notice. The notice was given by email on June 2, 2026, by Apex's Program Manager, Priya Raman, to Morgan's Project Contact, Owen Tremblay [1]. The email described the event and the expected delivery of the replacement Units on June 10, 2026 [1].

However, the documents do not confirm whether the notice was given within five Business Days after Apex first became aware of the Force Majeure Event. The flood occurred on May 21, 2026, and the notice was sent on June 2, 2026, which may or may not be within the required five Business Days [1].

Additionally, the notice must describe the Force Majeure Event, the obligations affected, its expected duration, and the steps taken to mitigate its effects [7]. The documents do not provide enough information to confirm whether the notice met these requirements.

turns.question: How much can Morgan claim in liquidated damages for the late delivery? Show the working.
turns.text:
The liquidated damages Morgan can claim for the late delivery are USD 55,800.

The Delivery Date was amended to May 20, 2026 [6]. The delivery was completed on June 10, 2026 [6]. The period of delay is 21 days, which equals exactly 3 weeks [6].

The weekly liquidated damages rate is 1.5% of the Total Contract Price, which is USD 1,240,000 [6]. For 3 weeks, the total liquidated damages are 3 × USD 18,600 = USD 55,800 [6].

The cap on liquidated damages is 10% of the Total Contract Price, which is USD 1,240,000 [6]. Since USD 55,800 is less than USD 124,000, the cap does not apply, and the total remains USD 55,800 [6].

The clause for liquidated damages was amended to increase the rate from 1% to 1.5% per week [5]. This amendment was signed and took effect on May 14, 2026 [5].

turns.question: What must a force majeure notice contain under the agreement, and when must it be given?
turns.text:
Under the agreement, a force majeure notice must state that it is given under clause 8.2 and must describe the event, the obligations affected, its expected duration, and the steps taken to mitigate it [2].

The notice must be given within five Business Days after the Affected Party first becomes aware of the Force Majeure Event [2].

turns.question: Which units were rejected, why, and which units replaced them?
turns.text:
The rejected units were IC450-1113 and IC450-1134. Unit IC450-1113 was rejected due to a cracked condenser housing, and Unit IC450-1134 was rejected due to a refrigerant leak at a brazed joint in circuit 2 [1].

turns.question: What case does the research memo rely on for the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause, and can we rely on it?
turns.text:
The research memo relies on the case of Larkspur Hydraulics Corp. v. Vantrell Fabrication Co., 284 A.3d 1176, 1183 (Del. 2022) for the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause. The memo states that Delaware courts will generally enforce a liquidated damages clause where the damages were difficult to estimate when the contract was made and the agreed amount is a reasonable forecast of the probable loss rather than a penalty [3].

The memo also notes that the parties recorded their agreement in clause 7.3 of the Services Agreement that the amounts are "a reasonable pre-estimate of those losses and not a penalty" [3]. However, the memo does not provide any further details about the case or its applicability beyond this citation. The documents in this matter do not answer whether we can rely on this case for the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause.

turns.question: What delivery date did the Services Agreement originally set?
turns.text:
The Services Agreement (DEMO) originally set the Delivery Date as May 15, 2026. This is stated in clause 4.2 of the agreement, which provides: "The Supplier shall deliver all Units to the Delivery Point on or before May 15, 2026" [2].

Later, Amendment No. 1 changed the Delivery Date to May 20, 2026. This is confirmed in the Notice of late delivery and claim (DEMO), which states: "Clause 1.1 of Amendment No. 1 replaced clause 4.2 with a Delivery Date of May 20, 2026" [4]. The amendment was signed by both parties and took effect on May 14, 2026 [6].

The original Delivery Date, as set in the Services Agreement (DEMO) before the amendment, was therefore May 15, 2026.

turns.question: Is that still the date?
turns.text:

Additionally, the amendment states that "the Delivery Date for all purposes of the Agreement, including clauses 7 and 11.3 of the Agreement, is May 20, 2026" [3].

Apex also confirms that the Delivery Date, as amended by Amendment No. 1, is May 20, 2026 [2]. Therefore, the date has been officially changed and remains May 20, 2026.

turns.question: When did Apex dispatch the units?
turns.text:
The documents state that Apex dispatched the units on May 10, 2026. This is supported by the email from Priya Raman, Program Manager at Apex, which stated the planned dispatch date as May 10, 2026 [6].

Additionally, the Services Agreement, as amended by Amendment No. 1, set the Delivery Date as May 20, 2026 [9]. However, the actual delivery of the units occurred on May 15, 2026, as stated by Apex in their response to the claim [4].

turns.question: And when did they arrive?
turns.text:
The delivery date of the units was May 20, 2026, as amended by Amendment No. 1. [1] This amendment was signed by both parties on May 14, 2026, and took effect on that date. [1]

However, there is conflicting evidence regarding when the units actually arrived. Witness A recalled that the units arrived at Dock 3 on May 12, 2026. [2] Witness B confirmed that the units arrived on May 15, 2026, at 07:40. [5] Apex also stated that all forty units arrived on May 15, 2026, as shown by carrier records and confirmed by Morgan's email. [4]

Despite this, the amended delivery date was May 20, 2026. [1]

turns.question: Does anyone remember it differently?
turns.text:
The documents indicate that Mr. Pell and Ms. Achterberg remember the delivery date differently.

Mr. Pell recalled that the units arrived at Dock 3 on May 12, 2026, stating, "I'm fairly sure it was the 12th. It was the week of our quarterly cycle count, and I remember the trucks coming in first thing, before eight" [4].

Ms. Achterberg, on the other hand, knew the original delivery date was May 15, 2026, and learned that it had been moved to May 20, 2026 by an amendment [3].
